import itertools
from pysat import SATSolver
from pysat.formula import CNF

n = 8
edges = {}
idx = 0
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i+1, n):
        edges[(i,j)] = idx
        idx += 1

print("Total edges:", idx)

cnf = CNF()

# For each 4-set, at least one edge is blue (1) => not all red (0)
# Clause: OR_{i<j in set} x_{i,j}  (since x=1 means blue)
for quad in itertools.combinations(range(n), 4):
    clause = []
    for i, j in itertools.combinations(quad, 2):
        clause.append(edges[(i,j)] + 1)  # pysat uses 1-indexed
    cnf.append(clause)

# For each 3-set, at least one edge is red (0) => not all blue (1)
# Clause: OR_{i<j in set} ~x_{i,j}  (i.e., at least one is 0)
for tri in itertools.combinations(range(n), 3):
    clause = []
    for i, j in itertools.combinations(tri, 2):
        clause.append(-(edges[(i,j)] + 1))
    cnf.append(clause)

print("Number of clauses:", len(cnf.clauses))

solver = SATSolver()
solver.append_formula(cnf)
status = solver.solve()
print("Status:", status)
if status:
    model = solver.get_model()
    # model is list of literals (1-indexed)
    # Convert to 0/1 for each edge in order
    sol = [0]*28
    for lit in model:
        var = abs(lit) - 1
        val = 1 if lit > 0 else 0
        sol[var] = val
    print("Solution:", sol)
    # Verify
    # Check red K4
    ok = True
    for quad in itertools.combinations(range(n), 4):
        all_red = True
        for i,j in itertools.combinations(quad,2):
            if sol[edges[(i,j)]] == 1: # blue
                all_red = False
                break
        if all_red:
            print("Found red K4:", quad)
            ok = False
    # Check blue K3
    for tri in itertools.combinations(range(n), 3):
        all_blue = True
        for i,j in itertools.combinations(tri,2):
            if sol[edges[(i,j)]] == 0: # red
                all_blue = False
                break
        if all_blue:
            print("Found blue K3:", tri)
            ok = False
    if ok:
        print("Solution verified!")
else:
    print("UNSAT")
